story.title: Four steps, one idea: the plan should fit you, not the other way round.

steps.title: Getting to know you
steps.body: We talk about what you eat, how you live and what you enjoy. There are measurements too — but your story comes first.

steps.title: Planning
steps.body: A weekly plan built from food you like, around your hours. No banned list — clear, realistic portions.

steps.title: Follow-up
steps.body: Regular check-ins adjust the plan to your real life. One hard week doesn't mean the plan is over.

steps.title: Outcome
steps.body: The goal may be a number. The real goal is habits that last after the plan ends, and a calmer relationship with food.

wizard.title: What brings you here?
wizard.lead: Pick one; with four more questions we’ll work out your first steps. No sign-up.

tools.title: Numbers help when you're curious.
tools.lead: Estimate your daily energy needs or find where to start in five questions. Free, no sign-up.
tools.calcBody: Resting metabolism, daily needs and a macro split — live.
tools.wizardBody: Five short questions. Three first steps that suit you.
tools.footnote: No sign-up, no fee. Calculations run in your browser.

recipes.title: In the kitchen this week
recipes.lead: Real kitchens, real timings. Every recipe's nutrition is calculated from its ingredients.

week.title: What does a week of meals look like?
week.lead: Flip a card to see the day's meals and energy split. This is an example; your plan is built around you.

guides.title: Short, sourced, useful.
guides.lead: Common nutrition questions, answered without hype and with sources.

contact.title: Write. Let's talk.
contact.lead: The first step is a message. Tell us your goal, your problem or just what you're curious about; you'll get a reply as soon as possible.

apply.title: Lasting change takes time.
apply.lead: Programmes run for at least 3 months; there is no one-month option. Tell us about yourself in a short application and we will build the right plan together.

items.q: Do I need to be a certain weight to start?
items.a: No. Nutrition counselling doesn't start at a weight threshold; wanting to improve your energy, digestion, routine or simply your relationship with the kitchen is enough.

items.q: Will I have to give up foods I love?
items.a: Plans aren't built on banned lists. The food you love stays in the plan — we talk about portion, frequency and context.

items.q: I have a chronic condition or I'm pregnant. Can I still apply?
items.a: Yes, but in these situations your nutrition plan should be coordinated with your doctor. Please share your health status and any medication in the first session.

items.q: How does my programme reach me?
items.a: Your programme arrives on your phone as a private, secure link. No account or login needed; you can print it or save it as a PDF.

items.q: How are sessions arranged and what do they cost?
items.a: For current session options and fees, send a message on WhatsApp or through the contact form.

suggestions.skip_breakfast: Focus on starting breakfast rather than making it big: an egg, a slice of wholegrain bread and a tomato is enough.
suggestions.late_eating: Try moving dinner 30 minutes earlier and add a small, protein-rich afternoon snack.
suggestions.snacking: Don't ban snacking; plan it. Choose one or two set snacks a day (yoghurt, fruit, a handful of nuts).
suggestions.eat_out: When eating out, aim to fill half the plate with vegetables, plus a protein and a small portion of carbohydrate.
suggestions.low_veg: Add one vegetable to every meal: tomato and cucumber at breakfast, a salad at lunch, a bowl of cooked vegetables at dinner.
suggestions.sweet_drinks: Start by swapping one sugary drink a day for sparkling water or water with lemon.
suggestions.low_water: Keep a visible bottle of water on your desk and drink a glass with every meal.
suggestions.irregular: Fix the times first: three meals at roughly the same times each day, plus a snack if needed.
suggestions.default_1: Try filling half your plate with vegetables, a quarter with protein and a quarter with whole grains.
suggestions.default_2: Two days a week, plan dinner ahead and cook it at home.
suggestions.default_3: Tie drinking water to a habit: a glass before every meal.

help.title: How to use the panel
help.lead: A picture and step-by-step explanation for every page. Always available from the menu and the command palette.

ui.pageHelp: How do I use this page?

dashboard.title: Overview
dashboard.lead: Your practice today on one screen: what is waiting, the figures and your tasks.
steps: The icons in the greeting row show what is waiting for you today. Hover to see what each one is; click to open the page.
The boxes give the basic figures: clients, appointments, payments received.
Change the period with the filter at the top right of each chart (last month, 3 months, all time).
Tasks: write what needs doing and give it a date. On a task linked to a client, tick “Show to the client” and they tick it in their own panel; yours then says “Done by the client”.

clients.title: Clients
clients.lead: The list of all your clients. Click one to open their profile.
steps: Search: type a name, e-mail, phone or tag; the list narrows as you type.
“New client” opens the full form. “Quick add” needs only a name and a contact; complete the rest later.
Click a card to open the profile. The card shows the latest measurement and the consent status.
Switch between cards and table. Clients moved to the archive stay under “Archived” and can be restored.

profile.title: Client profile
profile.lead: Everything about one client in tabs: measurements, notes, files, programmes, payments and the client’s own records.
steps: Move between the tabs to open each section. To keep one open separately, use the tab strip at the top.
Measurements: enter weight and circumferences at each appointment; the chart and progress to goal update by themselves.
Tracking and messages: the client’s daily record (water, energy, movement), food diary, “Plan followed (7 days)” and the lab reports they sent.
In the payments tab, define a package and record what you receive with “Take payment”. The client sees the package and payments in their panel; never your notes.

invite.title: Invite a client to the portal
invite.lead: To let a client into their own portal you give them a single-use invitation link.
steps: In the profile press “Create invitation link”. For security the link is shown only then; if you close it without copying, create a new one.
“Send with WhatsApp” opens the link in a ready-made message.
If the client is with you, they can scan the QR code with their phone.
For a forgotten password give a “Password reset link”. “Close portal access” deletes the sign-in account; the records they entered stay with you.

programs.title: Programmes
programs.lead: Build eating programmes here, keep them as templates and assign them to clients.
steps: Days: create one with “Add day”, multiply similar days with “Copy day”.
Daily targets: enter energy and macro targets; the day total is shown against them.
Meals: search a food or recipe, drag it onto a meal or click it; set the amount, add a note.
A client sees a programme only when both are true: it is assigned to that client and its status is “Active”. Drafts are never shown to the client.

messages.title: Messages
messages.lead: Your conversations with every client on one page.
steps: Pick a client in the list on the left; the conversation opens on the right.
Write your reply in the box at the bottom and send it.
The paperclip sends a file. Lab reports and photos a client sends appear in the conversation and among the files in their profile.
Clients with unread messages are marked in the list; the number in the menu is the total.

appointments.title: Appointments
appointments.lead: The calendar where you plan your meetings.
steps: “Add appointment”: choose the client, date and time, length and type.
Switch between list and calendar; move through the weeks with the arrows.
Click an appointment to edit it or update its status. Meetings marked as done count as used sessions in the client’s package.
An appointment you plan shows in the client’s portal at once: as “Next meeting” on Today and on “Visits & payments”, with an “Add to calendar” button.

payments.title: Payments
payments.lead: A summary of what you received and what is still owed.
steps: Choose the period with the date filter; every figure follows it.
The boxes: amount received, number of payments, and what is owed on open packages.
Search finds a record by client, package or note.
A new payment is recorded from the payments tab of the client’s profile with “Take payment”, and is listed here.

leads.title: Requests
leads.lead: Applications from the form on your site arrive here.
steps: The tabs at the top and the date filter separate new, contacted and archived requests.
“Convert to client” turns a request into a client record in one step.
Click a request to see the person’s answers in the wizard and the consent they gave.
After calling, “Mark as contacted”; “Archive” those who are not interested.

explorer.title: Client explorer
explorer.lead: For going through your active clients one card at a time.
steps: Move between clients with the arrows or the ← → keys.
The ring shows how close the client is to their goal.
Latest measurements, active programme, next appointment and the pinned note are on the same card.
“Open profile” goes to the client’s full page.

content.title: Recipes, guides, foods
content.lead: The content published on your site and the food database you use in programmes.
steps: Filter the list: all, published or draft.
Start with “New recipe” or “New guide”. For foods you enter the values per 100 g and the units.
Click a row to open the editor. The content-language tabs hold a separate text for each language.
“Publish” puts the content on the site, “Unpublish” takes it back. Arabic and French content is not published until a native speaker marks it “Reviewed”.

settings.title: Settings
settings.lead: Your profile, what the site says about you, and security.
steps: Profile and site content: your name, biography, contact details and social accounts.
Choose the panel language and the content language here.
Security: change your password (at least 10 characters).
Turn on two-step verification: scan the QR code with your authenticator app and enter the code. Recommended, since you hold client data.

shortcuts.title: Shortcuts and tabs
shortcuts.lead: Ways to move quickly around the panel.
steps: Tabs: open a new one with the + at the top and keep several clients or pages open at once. Right-click a tab for the closing options.
Ctrl K (⌘ K on a Mac) opens the command palette: type a page, a client or a command.
Ctrl B narrows and widens the menu; the arrow in the menu does the same.
At the bottom of the menu: day / night theme, panel language and “Install as an app”.

tour.title: First time here?
tour.text: A short guide shows how each page is used, with screenshots and step by step. You can also open it any time from “How to use it” in the menu.

help.title: How to use the portal
help.lead: What each page is for and how to use it, with pictures and step by step. You can come back any time from “How to use it” in the menu.

ui.pageHelp: How do I use this page?

today.title: Today
today.lead: The page you open first each day. Keep the day’s record here and reach your dietitian from here. Tasks from your dietitian also appear here: tap the tick beside one when it is done.
steps: The day’s record: tap “Glass” or “Bottle” for water, tick your habits, choose your energy and movement, and enter your weight if you weighed yourself. Every tap is saved by itself.
The ring shows how much of today’s record is filled in. The rows beside it tell you which part is still missing.
In your plan today: the next meal is marked. Tap “I ate this” and the meal goes into your diary.
The dietitian card: read their last message, write a short note, send a lab report or a file, or send a summary of your week in one tap.

program.title: Plan
program.lead: The eating plan your dietitian prepared for you. It appears here once your dietitian has made it active.
steps: Days: tap a day at the top to open its plan. Today comes selected.
Daily targets: your energy, protein, carbohydrate and fat targets.
Meals: what to eat at each meal, how much, and your dietitian’s note if there is one.
“Print / PDF” puts the plan on paper or saves it to your phone.

diary.title: Diary
diary.lead: Where you write what you ate, meal by meal. It does not need to be perfect; your dietitian compares it with your plan.
steps: Pick a day: tap one in the strip at the top. You can fill in past days too.
“Add” searches foods and recipes; enter the amount. If you ate the planned meal, “Add from program” is enough.
Photo and note: add a photo to a meal or a short note such as “ate out”. Only you and your dietitian see them.
The day’s total: the energy and nutrients of what you ate, next to your target.

progress.title: Progress
progress.lead: Your records over time. The numbers are only one part of the journey.
steps: Summary boxes: your latest weight, the change since the start, and your goal.
Time range: choose how many days the chart shows.
Weight chart: your own entries and the measurements taken at appointments, drawn together. “Show as table” if you prefer.
Habits and water: which days you did what over the last weeks, square by square.

week.title: Weekly summary
week.lead: Your last seven days on one page: how many days you recorded, how much water, how much movement.
steps: The boxes at the top give the week’s totals: days recorded, average water, movement, weight change and how closely you followed the plan.
By day: each day’s water, record and movement. Tap a day to open its diary.
Day by day: the same information row by row. Tap a day’s name to go to its diary.
“Write to your dietitian” lets you leave a note about your week.

messages.title: Messages
messages.lead: Where you write to your dietitian. It is not a live chat; they reply when they are available. In a medical emergency call your local emergency number.
steps: Write your message in the box at the bottom and send it.
The paperclip sends a lab result or a photo (PDF, JPEG, PNG, WebP; up to 10 MB).
Ready openers: with an empty box, buttons such as “I have a question:” start the message for you.
Your dietitian’s replies appear on the left; a red mark in the menu tells you a new one arrived.

care.title: Appointments and payments
care.lead: The meetings your dietitian planned for you and the state of your package. This page is for information only.
steps: The next meeting is on top: date, time, type and length. To change the time, message your dietitian.
“Add to calendar” saves the meeting to the calendar on your phone or computer.
Your package: sessions used, price, paid and remaining.
Payments: the payments your dietitian recorded, with dates and amounts.

files.title: My files
files.lead: Every file shared with your dietitian in one list, without searching the conversation.
steps: “Send a file” takes you to Messages; the paperclip there adds a lab report or a photo.
Sent by me: the reports and photos you sent, newest first.
From my dietitian: the documents your dietitian sent you.
Tap a file to open it. Only you and your dietitian can see the files.

shopping.title: Shopping list
shopping.lead: A list made from the foods in your plan. Use it when you go shopping.
steps: Days: choose which days go into the list. For a few days of shopping, turn the others off.
List: each food once, with its total amount or how many times it appears in the plan.
Tap what you have bought to tick it. Ticks stay on this device.
“Copy” takes the list for your notes app or a message; “Print” puts it on paper.

account.title: My account

steps: Your details: your name and e-mail. If something needs changing, your dietitian updates it.
Panel language: use the panel in Turkish, English, Arabic or French.
Change password: type the new password twice and save.
Your data: download all your records as one file, or withdraw your consent.

apply.title: Let’s work together
apply.lead: Four short steps: the programme, you, your health background and how to reach you. The dietitian reviews your application and gets back to you on the channel you choose.

rule.title: At least 3 months.
rule.body: Eating habits do not change in a few weeks, so there is no one-month programme. Programmes run for 3, 6 or 12 months.

send.body: Your answers are saved in a panel only the dietitian can see.

items.a: Eating habits do not change in a few weeks; a plan needs time to fit your life and for the change to last. That is why programmes run for 3, 6 or 12 months and there is no one-month programme.
The dietitian reviews your application and gets back to you on the channel you chose (WhatsApp, phone or email); the first meeting is planned together.
Only the dietitian. Health questions are optional; what you share is used with your explicit consent to assess your application, and kept in a panel only the dietitian can see.
Both are possible. Choose in the form, or say “Either”.
Your answers stay in this tab, even if you reload the page. Health answers are not kept this way; you choose them again.

cookies.title: Your cookie choice
cookies.body: This site only uses the cookies it needs to work (language, sign-in). No advertising or analytics cookies. If anything optional is ever added, your choice is checked first; you can change it at any time from the bottom of the site.

plan.title: A plan made for you.
